statement: The Harbor research program is the part of the whitepaper that has to be proved, measured, or admitted open rather than argued. Seven conference-form papers carry the theorems; a results index says where each executed result lives in the book; a manifest names every mechanized artifact and whether it runs in CI; pre-registered studies take the questions the book cannot settle from its own results; and a ledger keeps every review objection with what was done about it. This file is what the website renders. It is checked against the index, the manifest, the ledger, and the repository on every pull request.

deepDives.oneLine: Kofman and Lawarrée pose the unbounded-collateral regress as an open question; the tower theorem answers it. The pass also found and fixed an arithmetic defect in the paper's own C=1 counter-case.

The rumoured same-year preprint is real and orthogonal; the real prior problem is Basin et al. (TISSEC 2013). Two correctness bugs against Schneider's theorem were found and fixed; the Ramadge–Wonham identification survives.

The tractable-then-NP-complete shape is already mapped by the compliance-checking line; the specific fragment and conflict-freedom as the decision problem survive as novel. A wrong-strictness iff stated three ways was unified.
The citation flagged as fabricated is real and irrelevant, excluded on relevance. Herlihy–Shavit and three foundational citations were added to close a real omission.
Each pillar narrows to a known result the paper mostly pre-concedes; one corollary used an invalid composition bound and was rewritten to the model it holds for.
No prior work proves the theorems, but Theorem 2a is Akerlof's lemons result and was renamed, and a plotted crossing the paper's own figure contradicted was corrected.

wrongTurns.lesson: The meter charged bits for tie-breaking, not identification, and produced 8 of 14 spurious floor violations. The fixed experiment is the one the paper cites.
Zoom was tested in the dense-flag regime, where it cannot help, and showed an apparent 0.5× advantage. The frontier only exists where flags are sparse.
Computed the dimension of the abstract sheaf's first cohomology, which does not depend on the data, instead of the obstruction of the observed assignment.
A vector-stalk wrapper whose random restrictions were surjective, killing the cokernel, with inconsistent masking and the wrong partition detector. Rebuilt from a minimal mechanism proof.

studies.title: Is the single-writer rail the right collaboration model, and is the enforcement point below the agent the right substrate?
studies.question: The kernel chapter argues that confinement needs an enforcement point below the agent. It does not know whether the single-writer rail is also the right way for several agents to share one repository, against a worktree per agent with a merge queue. The rail is a design invariant until this study reports.
studies.design: Real commit histories from three public repositories replayed through six coordination substrates (uncoordinated tree; advisory claims with a bypass rate; the enforced rail; worktree per agent with a merge queue; the rail with region claims) at 2, 4, 8, and 16 agents, cooperative and impatient, twenty seeds per cell. Five metrics fixed before the first run.

hypotheses.title: Confinement
hypotheses.statement: Torn-tree incidents under advisory claims grow with the bypass rate, the agent count, and file overlap, and are zero under every enforced substrate. If this fails for the rail, the harness is wrong, not the theory.

hypotheses.title: The real question
hypotheses.statement: At low overlap the merge queue matches or beats the rail on throughput and time to land. At high overlap the rail beats the merge queue on wasted work by at least a factor of two and matches it on throughput within 20%. If the merge queue matches or beats the rail on every metric in every high-overlap cell, the book demotes the rail to a confinement mechanism.

hypotheses.title: Enforcement, or only confinement
hypotheses.statement: The shim used exactly as designed and the enforced rail are indistinguishable on every coordination metric. If so, the argument for the enforcement point is confinement alone, and the book says so.

hypotheses.title: Granularity
hypotheses.statement: Region claims recover at least half of the rail's throughput deficit against the merge queue at high overlap, where a deficit exists.

studies.notRunnableHere: S1, the substrate cost and controllability table (bare process, seccomp and Landlock, gVisor, Firecracker) needs KVM or unprivileged user namespaces and runs on the author's machine.
studies.reportRule: One report whatever the outcome. If H2's kill condition holds, the report says so in its first sentence and the kernel chapter and front matter are amended in the same pull request. Numbers reach the book as verified only when the pinned corpora and seeds regenerate them.

plannedLifts.title: Lift the work-unit machine to TLA+ and Apalache
plannedLifts.statement: The 536-state work-unit machine is checked exhaustively by a Python model with mutation-proven guards. The lift restates it in TLA+ and checks it with Apalache so the kernel's invariants join the same estate as the relay and the ledger.

plannedLifts.title: Lift sealed-room noninterference to Isabelle
plannedLifts.statement: Noninterference holds under every interleaving to depth seven in the finite model. The unbounded statement is an unwinding argument, and the lift is to state it in Isabelle against the Archive of Formal Proofs' noninterference library.

plannedLifts.title: Discharge the three admitted steps in the Merkle binding proof
plannedLifts.statement: The bond ledger's Merkle binding is sketched in EasyCrypt with three admitted tactics, and EasyCrypt does not run in CI. The artifact is graded partial in the manifest until the admits are discharged and the tool is pinned.

plannedLifts.title: The minimum viable take-rate
plannedLifts.statement: The economy chapter prices the three-sided market on one conserving ledger. It does not yet derive the smallest platform take that keeps the market open, which is the result the pricing page would have to cite.

openProblems.title: Authority transfer between harbors
openProblems.statement: Writer epochs appear in the book only as a revocation mechanism. There is no procedure for freezing a harbor's authority, exporting it, importing it under verification, activating the new epoch, and rolling back by epoch. The Chartroom decision cannot be graded until it exists. This is the largest silence.

openProblems.title: The release ledger in the other direction
openProblems.statement: The ledger meters the customer's data leaving the sealed room. The provider's implementation leaking through the customer's queries is the same ledger with the roles swapped, and it is unwritten. No provider-IP claim can be graded before it is.

openProblems.title: Dispute windows, partial work, and refunds
openProblems.statement: The Bonded Commons gives conservation and two-of-three settlement; the economy gives prices. Neither gives the time and arithmetic of a dispute: how long a window stays open, what a partially delivered work order is worth, and how a refund conserves.

openProblems.title: A constitution for the registry
openProblems.statement: Who may suspend a publisher, under what review, with what appeal. The book has the bond and the audit; it does not have the emergency path.

openProblems.title: One label scheme for product, roadmap, and book
openProblems.statement: The product's five evidence labels, the book's five assurance modes, and its four statement kinds should be one table, so that a product badge, a roadmap item, and a chapter claim speak the same words.

openProblems.title: Equivocation by a coalition on a cycle
openProblems.statement: The consistency radius certifies a lower bound on any single equivocator's lie. Two liars placed on one cycle can cancel to a residual of zero, measured at 6×10⁻¹⁵. Detecting coordinated equivocation needs a different invariant.

openProblems.title: Context paging against an adaptive pin adversary
openProblems.statement: The paging bound holds against a pin oracle corrupted at a fixed rate with repair on touch. An adversary that adapts its corruptions to the operator's access pattern is stronger than greedy and is untested.

openProblems.title: An incremental conflict checker for the tractable fragment
openProblems.statement: Conflict-freedom inside the tractable fragment is decided in polynomial time with a witness, from scratch. An amortized checker that updates the witness as one policy changes is stated, not built.

results.title: Read-poverty and the information floor
results.oneBreath: A human overseeing a fleet of software agents reads digests, not transcripts, and any digest that guarantees catching all k load-bearing artifacts among N while opening only m must carry at least log2 C(N,k) - log2 C(m,k) bits.

results.title: Split-digest theorem (comonotone characterization)
results.oneBreath: A scalar head serves a reader iff ranking by it realizes that reader's optimal selection at every budget; one head serves two readers iff their preference orders are comonotone, and the successor and operator readers provably are not.

results.title: The derived regret head
results.oneBreath: Inspect iff C_miss(x)*a(x) >= c_att + C_fa*(1-a(x)); the folklore ranking key stakes x irreversibility x anomaly is the Bayes-optimal surfacing rule iff anomaly is a calibrated posterior.

results.title: Digest-zoom Pareto frontier and the zoom-advantage theorem
results.oneBreath: A two-constraint rate-distortion program R(delta,f) prices misses separately from flag rate with a closed form for Bernoulli sources, and adaptive halving finds the k criticals inside F flagged items in at most 2k*ceil(log2(F/k))+4k group opens versus F flat.

results.title: Hypervisor enforceability = supervisory control
results.oneBreath: A safety policy is regimentable (preventable pre-effect) by an agent hypervisor iff it is controllable in the Ramadge-Wonham sense with respect to the uncontrollable event set; gate the channel, never the token.

results.title: Sheaf verdict: cohomology of equivocation
results.oneBreath: In gossip of signed logs, the least-squares completion residual detects a single equivocator's split-view lie beyond pairwise comparison iff the unchecked edge lies on a cycle of the visible coordinate subgraph, and its endpoints' reports are relayed to the analyst.

results.title: Inspection tower: reputation is amortized verification
results.oneBreath: A bonded judge is deterred iff rho*d*B >= G; auditors sampled sealed from C disjoint cliques make bribery all-or-nothing and unprofitable below corrupt value C*B, so finite bond capital certifies a tower of logarithmic depth, and lifetime audit spend falls from Theta(T) to Theta(log T) or O(1) as reputation accumulates.

results.title: The work-unit machine
results.oneBreath: The state machine (phase, policy, receipt, epoch/holder/stale-token, grants-with-parentage, effect journal, idempotency journal, settlement) satisfies six safety invariants in all 536 reachable states, each guard shown load-bearing by mutation.

results.title: Sealed-room noninterference
results.oneBreath: With declared release g(s) = s mod 2, Erin's observations are identical whenever g(s)=g(s') for every interleaving, and may differ only at explicit gate-release steps otherwise -- noninterference modulo declassification, verified exhaustively to depth 7 on the finite clean-room model.

results.title: Epsilon-conservation of the release ledger
results.oneBreath: The release ledger's only spending transition atomically appends the record and adds the spend, so every reachable state satisfies sigma = sum of the ledger's epsilons and sigma <= epsilon_max, including under concurrent invocation.

results.title: Canary detection power and SPRT latency
results.oneBreath: Independent per-canary misses turn k smuggled canaries into detection probability 1 - beta^k; Wald's sequential probability ratio test against the permutation null turns leak intensity into an expected time-to-detection with realized error rates at or below target.

results.title: No-mint reputation inheritance
results.oneBreath: Discount-and-split as transfer -- the child receives a discounted, debited share of each source's spend -- keeps total live creditable reputation below total witnessed value under any sequence of forks, merges, chains, or re-derivation cycles.

results.title: Engine substitution and resurrection soundness
results.oneBreath: Unattested, the period-2 price never depends on the actual engine so swapping to a cheap one always pays; daemon-attested engine ids flip the incentive to the planner's efficiency rule at zero audit stake, and sanction-respecting reputation survives provider migration under three named clauses, each individually load-bearing.

results.title: Costly-escalation threshold equilibrium and the debit tuning band
results.oneBreath: A strictly increasing escalation payoff gives a unique separating threshold u*(delta); the feasible debit set between the alarm-fatigue wall and the distress-silencing wall is an interval that can be empty, in which case the honest fix is capacity or evidence quality, not tuning.

results.title: Queueing specialization boundary and the succession price
results.oneBreath: Sole ownership weakly dominates the pool iff the skill premium clears the exact Erlang-C boundary g_A(rho,c), falsifying the whitepaper's proposed threshold in both directions; with mortality and succession, pooling dominates at every skill premium once xi/eta exceeds D* = etaK/(1-etaK).

results.title: Context paging with an untrusted pin oracle
results.oneBreath: Landlord's k/(k-h+1) competitiveness against offline OPT imports to variable-size context spans; a pin oracle corrupted on a psi fraction of consultations costs only an additive, linear psi*N*c_refetch penalty under repair-on-touch, sharing its corruption budget with R1's forgeable-feature budget.

results.title: Tractable deontic-conflict fragment and its NP-complete frontier
results.oneBreath: Inside a fragment of facts, definite Horn rules, ground deontic O/F rules, exclusive interval claims and difference constraints, conflict detection is polynomial and witness-producing; one expressive step out (disjunctive obligations under discharge choice) makes conflict-freedom NP-complete.

results.title: Consistency radius of the completion residual (CR-1/2/3)
results.oneBreath: The completion residual r is a certified lower bound on any injected lie (equality at the completion, closed form r = |s| * sqrt(1 - R_eff) for a single-edge lie), localizes to visible cycles through the equivocator, and computes as at most L scalar graph-Laplacian solves.

results.title: The probation cliff (front-loaded newcomer restriction)
results.oneBreath: Among all newcomer-restriction schedules with equal power to deter a short-horizon whitewasher, the maximally front-loaded feasible one -- a cliff, not a ramp -- uniquely minimizes the tax on honest newcomers.

results.title: Claim-signaling incentive compatibility (mechanized discount-factor thresholds)
results.oneBreath: In the corrected claim-signaling stage game, a grim trigger is subgame-perfect iff delta >= 1/3 and a three-round graduated trigger iff delta exceeds the unique real root delta* = 0.3425080314 of 2*delta^3+2*delta^2+2*delta-1=0, both mechanically checked by Z3 and TLA+/Apalache.
